chapter_title: Chương 134: Lừa người chơi nạp tiền mới là chân lí.

Chapter 137 Section 0134: Tricking Players into Spending is the Way to Go. The day after "Dialogue" aired, the awards for the 7th New Concept Composition Competition were presented.

Chen Guiliang sat below as a special guest and noticed that the press section was a little sparse this year.

Media attention had plummeted!

The way the first-place awards were set up was also quite abstract.

Last year, Group A and Group B each had 27 first-place winners.

This year, Group A had 40 first-place winners, while Group B had only 5.

Watching the winners go on stage to receive their awards, Chen Guiliang couldn't quite figure out what was going on.

Chen Guiliang asked Cao Wenxuan in a low voice, "Director Cao, the number of first-place awards for Group A and B seems a bit lopsided this year."

Cao Wenxuan explained, "The judging is strictly based on the quality of the essays. This year, there were many high-quality essays in Group A, but very few in Group B."

This meant the competition's pool of upcoming talent was failing.

Younger students who could write good essays were no longer bothering to sign up.

In another timeline, in the next New Concept Competition, the number of first-place winners in both Group A and B would drop to single digits.

This competition was, in essence, already dead!

In an effort to generate more buzz, the organizers even had Chen Guiliang come up to speak after the leaders' speeches. Of all the well-known young writers to emerge from New Concept, Chen Guiliang was the only one willing to show his support today.

What else could Chen Guiliang say? He gave a few simple remarks, thanking New Concept for providing him with a platform, congratulating this year's winners, and wishing the competition even greater success next year.

After the awards ceremony, Hu Weishi called Chen Guiliang over to the hallway. "That summer event has been confirmed. It's called the 'First Literary Intergenerational Communication Forum,' and it'll bring together old, middle-aged, and young writers for a dialogue. It's scheduled for around the end of July."

"I'll definitely be there," Chen Guiliang said.

The sound of a text message alert went off on his phone.

After reading the message, Chen Guiliang said, "Sorry, my girlfriend is here."

"Not staying for lunch?" Hu Weishi asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "I have to catch a flight."

Watching Chen Guiliang disappear down the hallway, Hu Weishi thought to himself: Just how many girlfriends does this guy have?

When Han Han chatted with Hu Weishi, he often bragged about having several girlfriends.

Chen Guiliang hurried downstairs and headed to the airport with Bian Guanyue.

Several times, Bian Guanyue wanted to speak her mind, but she swallowed the words each time they reached her lips.

Her cousin's words had indeed left Bian Guanyue feeling a little flustered. She felt she should be doing something, not just being a "little woman" by Chen Guiliang's side.

But she had no interest in doing business.

Right now, besides studying hard, it seemed there was nothing else she could do.

Bian Guanyue had tossed and turned last night, thinking for half the night before falling asleep.

She only knew how to sing Sichuan opera, but the Sichuan opera troupes had almost all been disbanded. Only a handful remained scattered across the country, barely surviving on government subsidies. Even famous performers were so poor they had to set up street stalls.

Putting aside whether it could make money, the key issue was the lack of an audience!

She had also studied vocal music for a few years and had specifically studied music theory for two and a half years.

Then, Bian Guanyue thought of "Mice Love Rice." The song had been incredibly popular recently. She wanted to write a song too, and release it as an online song.

But Bian Guanyue didn't want to be famous, or rather, she was a bit afraid of fame.

She planned to give herself a very ordinary stage name, the kind netizens would forget in an instant.

Yes, she had already thought of one. Her stage name would be "Li Jing."

It would be hard to remember even if you tried.

On the plane, Bian Guanyue finally couldn't hold it in any longer. "I want to compose a melody. Will you write the lyrics?"

"Why the sudden desire to write a song?" Chen Guiliang smiled.

Bian Guanyue said, "I want to find something to do. Online songs are really popular now, so I thought I'd try releasing one and see what happens."

"That's a great idea. You should have the courage to try," Chen Guiliang encouraged her.

Chen Guiliang didn't plan to just plagiarize a song for her.

Bian Guanyue's intention was to do something, not to become famous or make money.

After returning to Beijing, Bian Guanyue immediately went to buy a guitar and started trying to compose music in their rented apartment.

Chen Guiliang just watched with a smile, not interfering at all. He knew what this silly girl was thinking.

She felt a little insecure, afraid that her boyfriend was leaving her further and further behind!

Leaving her to fiddle with her music in the apartment, Chen Guiliang went to the company by himself.

"Well, look who it is. So CEO Chen still remembers how to come back," Guo Feng said, having learned to be sarcastic from Senior Sister Ao.

Chen Guiliang replied, "I was afraid you'd be lonely. Otherwise, I would have gone back to my hometown long ago."

Xie Yang also chimed in, "He definitely came back to supervise our work. You can't trust the words of a capitalist."

Chen Guiliang said, "I've already changed my QQ name to 'Little Boy Under the Streetlight.' If I ever exploit you in the future, just hang me from a streetlight."

He then went straight to Ao Yanchen's workstation. "How many Taobao shops have you contacted?"

Ao Yanchen, typing away on QQ, said while staring at the screen, "Over two hundred Taobao shops have agreed to help us sell Legends of the Three Kingdoms. I'm still contacting more."

Chen Guiliang said, "Have them state in their Taobao shops that we will subsidize 8 yuan of the shipping fee for each order."

"We'll need to have a serious talk with the courier companies in the future," Ao Yanchen said.

At this time, there were about 300,000 shops on Taobao.

Shipping costs fluctuated greatly.

YTO Express was the cheapest, followed by STO Express, then SF Express, with China Post being the most expensive.

In terms of delivery addresses, the Jiangsu-Zhejiang-Shanghai region was the cheapest, followed by the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, then Fujian and Guangdong. For many areas, only China Post would deliver!

For example, in provinces like Xinjiang and Tibet, shipping fees started at 50 yuan, and you could only use China Post's EMS.

As for the cheapest, YTO Express, shipping started at 8 yuan for the Jiangsu-Zhejiang-Shanghai region, 10 yuan for Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, and 12 yuan for Fujian and Guangdong. For inland provinces like Sichuan, not only were the shipping fees extremely high, but they would only deliver to the provincial capital.

For slightly more expensive items, buyers preferred Taobao shops in the same city. They would bypass couriers and do offline transactions, agreeing to meet at a certain station where the seller would deliver the goods by bus...

Under these circumstances, only a very small number of shops offered free shipping, and even then, they would raise the price of the product.

A large number of customers would change their minds after choosing an item because the shipping fee was too expensive.

Chen Guiliang was really going all out to sell the cards by subsidizing 8 yuan for shipping.

After chatting with Ao Yanchen for a while, Chen Guiliang went to check the data for the online version of Legends of the Three Kingdoms.

Registered users: 248,000. Daily active users: 75,000. Payment rate: 3.7%.

The payment rate was quite high, mainly because the players of Legends of the Three Kingdoms were predominantly users with their own computers. In this era, those who could afford a computer weren't short on cash!

The number of registered users was growing quite fast, and the ratio of daily active users was rising. This indicated that most of the recently registered users were not college students, as college students generally didn't bring their computers home for the winter break.

It had been eight days since the payment function was launched, and the cumulative amount charged had surpassed the 200,000 yuan mark!

But most of this 200,000 yuan was from purchasing memberships, and mostly monthly memberships at that. For the next month, it was very likely they wouldn't spend another cent.

He still had to find ways to trick the players into spending money.

A monthly membership cost 18 yuan, which allowed free use of the Wind Pack generals and came with some free items. It also provided an experience and silver coin bonus, and added an extra general selection slot.

Chen Guiliang typed on the keyboard, writing down a plan to induce players to spend:

First, add the general card Yuan Shao, obtainable only through opening loot boxes. To be released after the new semester starts.

Of course, Chen Guiliang wouldn't make it too disgusting. If a player got a duplicate general from a loot box, it could be decomposed into universal general souls. A certain number of general souls could then be used to craft Yuan Shao.

Second, provide three free SanGuoShow avatars and general skins for members.

Third, add premium borders, SanGuoShow avatars, and general skins, obtainable only through opening treasure chests.

Fourth, enable the "throw eggs" and "send flowers" functions. Everyone knows how this works. But given the current technology and internet speeds, the special effects must be simplified as much as possible.

Chen Guiliang logged into QQ and clicked on the avatar of a friend named "Tiandao Qian."

This was Guan Zhiqiang's senior from his fourth year.

"Master, isn't the premium skin for Diao Chan drawn yet?" Chen Guiliang asked.
